notes: Gathered on 2026-11-18 with WebFetch (page text summarised by a small model, so figures are as that summary reported them) and WebSearch used only to find URLs. Every entry's source_url is a page that was fetched and read; facts seen only in search snippets are in gaps. No websummit.com, lu.ma, luma.com, meetup.com or eventbrite pages were fetched. Several hosts refused or failed and are recorded in gaps. Reviewed by startups.b@PrompTugal.dinis on 18 November 2026: the Granter and Neuraspace amounts, dates and investors re-read at their source pages and confirmed; Granter's round type is not stated there, so it is not called a seed round; the Ponda round was removed because Ponda is a British company.

entries.name: Portugal Ventures
entries.what: Venture capital investor in technology-based startups headquartered in Portugal, at pre-seed, seed and Series A, with tickets of up to EUR 6 million. The home page states EUR 283 million under management and, since 2012, 256 new companies and EUR 233.2 million invested. The page names no specific 2025 to 2026 investments.

entries.name: INEYE Therapeutics follow-on (Portugal Ventures)
entries.what: Portugal Ventures' news page reports a follow-on of EUR 250,000, co-invested with Insight Venture, bringing the total invested in the round to EUR 600,000. The initial EUR 100,000 was made in 2023 through Call INNOV-ID. The page does not state the company's base.

entries.name: Caixa Capital
entries.what: Venture capital and private equity manager. Direct investments are preferably in Series A and B rounds, in innovative, technologically differentiated companies. Indirectly it invests through a fund of funds, mainly in venture funds based in Portugal or run by Portuguese teams, plus international funds. The page states about EUR 360 million under management and does not disclose ticket sizes or deal counts.

entries.name: EDP Ventures
entries.what: Corporate venture arm of EDP investing in early-stage technology startups in the energy sector, as a minority investor from seed to Series B. The page states EUR 150 million under management, tickets of EUR 1 million to EUR 10 million and around 5 to 8 investments a year. It shows portfolio logos but no dated deals.

entries.name: Faber
entries.what: Early-stage venture firm investing from pre-seed to Series A, with a first ticket of up to EUR 2.5 million, in Southern Europe with selective investments elsewhere in Europe. Focus areas stated: deep tech (applied science and digital transformation) and climate and ocean tech. The page lists deals including ATMOS (EUR 25.7 million Series A, participating), ISPTech (EUR 5.5 million seed, participating) and Zymvol (EUR 3 million seed, led), without dates; fund size is not stated on the page.

entries.name: Faber Tech III
entries.what: Fund announced on 4 November 2024 with a EUR 60 million target and an initial close of EUR 31 million, backed by the NATO Innovation Fund, the European Investment Fund and Caixa Capital. It invests at pre-seed and seed, primarily in Southern Europe. First investments were in undisclosed startups in Portugal, Spain and the Netherlands (photonic chips, analog chip design, synthetic biology).
entries.amount: EUR 60 million target; EUR 31 million initial close

entries.name: Angels Way
entries.what: Community-run fund managed collectively by 436 small investors and regulated by the CMVM, investing in early-stage Portuguese technology startups. On 3 September 2026 the article reports 15 companies in the portfolio valued together at EUR 79.5 million, a target of 20 startups and a focus on AI solutions built for international markets. A 6 October 2025 article gives a maximum ticket of EUR 50,000 per startup and says the fund is one of those managed by OW Ventures.

entries.name: Angels Way: Courtmaster, Curiouz and WiseWorld
entries.what: Three AI startups added to the Angels Way portfolio, reported on 6 October 2025: Courtmaster (padel sports tech), Curiouz (AI for the vintage furniture market) and WiseWorld (AI soft-skills training and certification). Amounts per company are not given; the community's total rose to EUR 350,000 across seven startups in nine months.

entries.name: Angels Way: Lampsy, Intuitivo, Smashpro and UpSpeech
entries.what: Four new investments reported on 3 September 2026, taking the portfolio to 15 companies: Lampsy (AI lamp detecting epilepsy seizures, from Instituto Superior Tecnico), Intuitivo (teachers' administration platform, founded in Porto in 2021), Smashpro (SaaS for padel, tennis and pickleball clubs) and UpSpeech (multimodal AI for speech therapy). Amounts are not disclosed.

entries.name: Granter funding round
entries.what: Portuguese startup Granter raised EUR 1.6 million (total funding EUR 2 million) for an AI platform that helps SMEs and startups find public funding, prepare applications and manage funded projects. Led by 3XP Global's Impact Innovation Fund, under the Capitalisation and Resilience Fund managed by Banco Português de Fomento. The article does not state Granter's base city.

entries.name: Neuraspace financing
entries.what: Neuraspace, a Portuguese space technology company founded in 2020, secured EUR 15.6 million. Its AI platform helps satellite operators track space conditions and avoid collisions; it monitors more than 600 satellites. Investors named: Lince Capital, Explorer Investments and Armilar Venture Partners, plus funding under the Recovery and Resilience Plan. Article dated 5 August 2026; base city not stated.

entries.name: Musiversal Series A
entries.what: Music Business Worldwide reports a USD 6 million Series A for Musiversal, based in Lisbon, bringing total funding to USD 10 million. Led by Iberis Capital with Lince Capital participating; earlier seed investors named are Shilling Capital, Intersection Ventures, SBS Braga and LC Ventures. Funds are for expansion into the US.

entries.name: Banco Português de Fomento (group)
entries.what: State development bank. Its home page states EUR 13.4 billion mobilised for the economy and more than 35 thousand companies supported over 22 months of the mandate, and lists Portugal Ventures and Fomento FEI (linked to InvestEU) among group entities, with a 'Fundos sob Gestao' section. The page gives no figures for any venture or co-investment programme.
